one_month_reasoning: Inside the window to 2026-11-05: (1) Nokia's Q3 2026 report on 22 Oct 2026 (Q2 6-K, src 1). The 6-K guides Q3 net sales +3% to +7% q/q and comparable operating profit 'largely flat' from Q2 (EUR 434m) because of software revenue phasing, and says FY26 is on track for 'somewhat above the midpoint' of EUR 2.1-2.6bn. Because the guide is explicit and the stock is already 23.5x FY27 consensus, I take no directional view on the print. (I dropped the Infront Q3 consensus I used in round 1: nokia.com returned 403 on re-check, so I could not reconfirm it.) (2) FOMC on 28 Oct 2026: Kalshi 82.5% hold / 17.5% hike, Polymarket 83.5% / 16.5% (DeFi Rate, observed 6 Oct 3:26 PM ET, volume not shown, src 11). This is context only and does not move the ladder. Base rates: the last four report-day moves were +11.2% (23 Oct 2025, 5.55 to 6.17), -7.8% (29 Jan 2026, 6.82 to 6.29), +4.8% (23 Apr 2026, 9.86 to 10.33) and -5.3% (23 Jul 2026, 10.28 to 9.73). That is a mean absolute move of 7.3%, two up and two down (Twelve Data closes, src 9-10). Realized vol is 70% over 21 days and 65% over 63 days (own computation, src 9). Today's +6.3% (from a $10.20 prior close) came on a day when peers also rose: CIEN +13.2%, CSCO +4.8% and ANET +4.2% intraday on their StockAnalysis pages (src 25, 24, 26). I read it as a sector move and take no drift from it. The ladder is a lognormal mixture centred at $10.80 (essentially spot), with 80% at log-sd 0.17 and 20% at 0.27. The effective sd of about 0.19 matches 65% x sqrt(21/252) = 0.188. That puts P(>= spot) at 0.49.

fair_value.method: Blend, at ECB EUR/USD 1.1269: (a) a mix-weighted SOTP P/E of 17.0x on NTM-at-horizon comparable EPS EUR 0.4208 = EUR 7.15 = $8.06 (weight 0.65); (b) a CMD-based DCF valued at end-2027 = EUR 6.79 = $7.65 (weight 0.35). 0.65 x 8.06 + 0.35 x 7.65 = $7.92, 27% below the $10.84 brief price (a 6 Oct intraday price from the run brief; the official 6 Oct close was $10.975, StockAnalysis NOK history). 1 ADS = 1 share.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM EPS at Oct-2027 = 0.25 x FY27 consensus EUR 0.41 + 0.75 x FY28E EUR 0.4244 = EUR 0.4208. Multiple 17.0x = 39.3% of 2028E segment OP (Optical+IP) at CSCO 22.1x + 11.4% (Fixed) at 13.8x + 49.3% (MI) at ERIC 13.6x. EUR 0.4208 x 17.0 = EUR 7.15 x 1.1269 = $8.06

inputs_detail.derivation: StockAnalysis 'EPS Next Year: 0.41 from 0.34', financial currency EUR, updated 17 Sep 2026.

No public FY28 consensus. I cap at the CMD top end, as the supervisor flagged that my round-1 EUR 0.44 implied OP above it: (EUR 3.2bn top-end 2028 comparable OP + EUR 0.15bn financial income, the low end of the 2026 assumption) x (1 - 26.5%) / 5,801.886m = EUR 0.4244. Cross-check: FY27 consensus 0.41 already implies OP of about EUR 3.09bn (0.41 x 5.8019bn / 0.735 - 0.15), so the top end in 2028 is the consistent path.
Q2 2026 diluted weighted average shares (thousands: 5 801 886).
Midpoint of the FY26 comparable income tax rate assumption of ~26-27%.
Low end of the FY26 assumption of EUR 150-250m, held flat.

CMD: MI to 'grow from a base of EUR 1.5 billion'. I take +10% = EUR 1.65bn (judgment). Group common is EUR 150m by 2028. NI = 3.2 + 0.15 - 1.65 = EUR 1.70bn, which is consistent with the NI target margin of 13-17%.
H1 2026 NI sales: Optical 1,689 + IP 1,305 = 2,994 of 3,866 (Fixed 872). Profit is assumed pro rata to sales (judgment; Fixed is shrinking, -8% H1 cc, so this is conservative for Optical+IP).

CSCO CY27 P/E = 118.19 / 5.346. CSCO is the growth match. Its EPS growth is +18.8% FY27 and +9.2% FY28, against Nokia Optical+IP at 18-20% in 2026 (guide) and a 10-12% CAGR target for 2025-28. CIEN (37.3x, +65%) and ANET (41.4x, +26.5%) grow much faster at higher margins, so their multiples are not claimed. Sensitivity: 30x here gives 20.1x blended and a P/E leg of $9.51.
Median of the CY27 P/Es of the access peers CALX 15.16x, ADTN 13.14x and HLIT 13.81x.

0.393 x 22.11 + 0.114 x 13.81 + 0.493 x 13.59 = 16.96x, rounded to 17.0x. That is 12.5% above the 11-peer median of 15.1x and inside the 7.7-41.4x range. The premium is profit mix only (see comps_summary).
ECB reference rate for 2026-10-06.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: Valued at end-2027 (about the horizon). FCF 2028 = EUR 3.2bn x 70% = EUR 2.24bn, +5%/yr to 2032 (2.35, 2.47, 2.59, 2.72), terminal growth 3%, discount 9.54% (10Y 5.31% + ERP 4.23%, beta 1.0). PV of flows EUR 9.41bn + PV of terminal value EUR 27.19bn = EV EUR 36.60bn, + net cash EUR 2.776bn = EUR 39.38bn / 5.8019bn = EUR 6.79 = $7.65

inputs_detail.derivation: Top end of the CMD target of EUR 2.7-3.2bn by 2028. This is consistent with the P/E leg and with FY27 consensus already implying about EUR 3.09bn.
Midpoint of the CMD long-term 'free cash flow conversion from comparable operating profit of between 65% and 75%'.
Between the CMD NI sales CAGR target of 6-8% and MI 'grow from a base', with group common flat.
US 10Y par yield of 5.31% on 2026-10-05 + Damodaran implied ERP of 4.23% (January 2026), x beta 1.0 (judgment). Nokia has net cash, so WACC = cost of equity.
Below the 5.31% nominal 10Y yield; roughly long-run nominal GDP for a mature networking vendor.
At 30 June 2026, held flat to the horizon. I assume FCF to end-2027 is absorbed by dividends, restructuring cash and capacity investment, so no unverified build is used.
Q2 2026 diluted weighted average.
ECB reference rate for 2026-10-06.

bear.story: AI & Cloud optical/IP orders (EUR 2.8bn in Q2, src 1) prove lumpy, Network Infrastructure growth slows toward the CMD 6-8% path, and FY27 EPS is cut to about EUR 0.35. The market then prices Nokia like Ericsson at about 13x: 13 x 0.35 = EUR 4.55 = $5.13. This is the mean of the bottom quartile of my ladder ($5.16). Nokia's own history allows it: after its +89-100% trailing-12-month run into Sep-Dec 2007, the next 12 months were -51% to -64% (src 8).

base.story: FY26 lands somewhat above the EUR 2.35bn midpoint, FY27 EPS comes in near the EUR 0.41 consensus, and NTM EPS at the horizon is about EUR 0.42. The multiple gives back part, not all, of its AI-optical premium: about 20.8x, between my 17x mix-justified value and today's ~23x. 0.42 x 20.8 = EUR 8.74 = $9.85. This is the mean of the middle half of my ladder ($9.84).

bull.story: AI & Cloud order conversion and the new optical capacity (San Jose fab ramping from Q4 2026; Chandler InP production from early 2027; src 1) push NTM EPS to about EUR 0.50, above the CMD top end. The market pays a CIEN-like ~35x: 0.50 x 34.6 = EUR 17.3 = $19.5, above the June 2026 high of $17.45. This is the mean of the top quartile of my ladder ($19.53), so it includes the tail where the June spike repeats.

comps_summary.peer_range: 11 networking-systems vendors. P/E is on CY2027 consensus EPS: Dec-FY peers use FY27; June/July-FY peers (CSCO, EXTR, AVNW) are calendarized from their FY27 and FY28 consensus; CIEN and HPE use FY27 ending Oct-27 (10 of 12 months overlap, FY28 not public). Range 7.65x (AVNW) to 41.44x (ANET), median 15.11x (HPE). TTM EV/EBITDA range 7.84x (ADTN) to 60.41x (CIEN), median 17.54x. NOK itself is at 23.46x FY27 (EUR 9.62 / 0.41) and 18.70x TTM EV/EBITDA (src 4). Prices are StockAnalysis page prices stamped 3:22-3:40 PM ET on 6 Oct 2026, not official closes. I did not use StockAnalysis 'Forward PE' because it mixes bases.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 17.0x NTM-at-horizon EPS: +12.5% vs the 15.1x median, inside the range, and well below NOK's own 23.5x.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: The premium is profit mix, not a call that Nokia will outperform its sector. About 39% of 2028E segment OP is in Optical+IP Networks. Those units grew +20% (Optical) and +9% (IP) cc in H1 2026 (src 1) and carry a CMD target of a 10-12% CAGR (src 2). That growth matches CSCO (EPS +18.8%/+9.2%), so they get CSCO's 22.1x. The rest (Fixed 11%, MI 49%) is valued at its own peers' 13.8x and 13.6x. The mix should persist through the horizon: these are Nokia's reported business units, NI's share is growing (NI guide +12-14% in 2026 vs MI with no growth guide), and the CMD targets run to 2028. No premium is given for the AI-optical sentiment that takes the stock from 17x to 23.5x. CIEN/ANET-level multiples would need CIEN/ANET-level growth and margins, and Nokia's Q2 NI margin was 8.1%.

thesis_break_reason: $6.44 = Ericsson's 13.59x FY27 multiple x NTM EPS EUR 0.4208 x 1.1269. At that price the market would give zero value to Nokia's Optical/IP growth mix and price it as a no-growth RAN vendor. Getting there with estimates intact is unlikely. More likely it would mean the earnings base broke: an FY26 guide cut below EUR 2.1bn, AI & Cloud orders reversing, or the 2028 EUR 2.7-3.2bn target being abandoned. My ladder puts about 21% on a close below it, mostly in exactly those cases.

catalysts.event: Q3 2026 report (guide: net sales +3-7% q/q, comparable OP largely flat vs Q2 EUR 434m; FY26 'somewhat above the midpoint' of EUR 2.1-2.6bn)
FOMC decision (Kalshi 82.5% hold, Polymarket 83.5% hold on 6 Oct; context only)
New San Jose optical fab begins ramping production later in Q4 2026
FOMC meeting (Kalshi ~74% odds of a hike by December on 6 Oct; context only)
Q4/FY2026 report and FY2027 outlook: first test of whether FY27 consensus (EUR 0.41, i.e. about EUR 3.09bn OP) holds
Indium Phosphide optical-component production at the Chandler, Arizona campus (NXP agreement; full acquisition closing Q1 2029)
Q1 and Q2 2027 reports: conversion of AI & Cloud orders (EUR 2.8bn intake in Q2 2026) into sales and NI margin progress toward 13-17%
Portfolio exits: FWA CPE sale to Inseego agreed; an Enterprise Campus Edge sale deemed highly probable (Q2 6-K)

key_uncertainties: Multiple: NOK is at 23.5x FY27 against a 15.1x median for the 11 systems peers on a CY27 basis. My 17.0x rests on profit mix. If the market keeps paying for AI optics, as it has all year, the fair value understates the price. Every +1x on the blended multiple is about +$0.47.
Optical+IP multiple choice: CSCO-like 22x vs a CIEN/ANET-like 37-41x is the largest swing factor. At 30x the P/E leg is $9.51, not $8.06.
Durability of AI & Cloud demand vs a capex digestion phase; the June-July 2026 drop from $17.45 to $8.37 shows how hard the cohort re-prices.
Earnings base: FY27 consensus EUR 0.41 already implies about EUR 3.09bn OP, the CMD 2028 midpoint a year early, and there is no public FY28 consensus.
Cash vs comparable earnings: Q2 FCF was -EUR 732m (H1 -EUR 104m), and EUR 800m of 2026 restructuring charges sit outside comparable EPS (src 1).
FX: EUR earnings and a USD ADR; a 5% EUR/USD move is about 5% on fair value (guidance assumes 1.14 vs ECB 1.1269).

Defense is not separately disclosed. The combined 'Mission Critical Enterprise & Defense' customer category was EUR 448m in Q2 2026, about 9% of group sales (448 / (434 / 0.090) is about 9.3%, estimate) (src 1). Nokia Defense is an incubation unit from the CMD (src 2). It is not in any number here.
reasoning: Supervisor findings I accepted after checking them at the source: ECB EUR/USD 1.1269 (ECB XML); the CMD caps 2028 OP at EUR 3.2bn and sets FCF conversion at 65-75% (CMD 6-K); the 10Y yield was 5.31% on 10/05 (Treasury CSV); the implied ERP is 4.23% (Damodaran). The supervisor was also right that my 23.5x peer median mixed bases and included component and materials names. I rebuilt the comps on one CY2027 basis and replaced GLW, LITE, COHR and MSI with genuine systems vendors (RBBN, HLIT, AVNW) to reach 11 peers. The median is 15.1x, matching the supervisor's 7-peer median. Valuation: NTM EPS EUR 0.4208 (FY27 consensus 0.41 blended with a top-end-capped FY28 of 0.4244). The multiple is 17.0x, built bottom-up from Nokia's reported business-unit mix: Optical+IP at CSCO 22.1x, Fixed at access peers 13.8x, MI at ERIC 13.6x. That gives $8.06. The DCF at 9.54% with 70% conversion gives $7.65, and the blend is FV $7.92. This is below the supervisor's $8.83 because I value NI at its sub-units' peers (22.1x / 13.8x) rather than a 26x haircut of the CIEN/ANET/CSCO median. Base rates (own computation, Twelve Data monthly, 310 windows 2000-2026): Nokia's median 12-month return is -8.4%, 5th/95th percentiles are -56%/+101%, log sd is 0.43, and P(up) is 0.44. After +80% trailing years (16 overlapping windows, only 2 episodes: 2007 and 2013-14) the median next-12-month return is -9.9% with 37.5% up. Small sample, but it leans the same way as valuation. Realized vol is 65% over 63 days and 71% over 129 days. Ladder: from FV to price. Judgment: valuation gaps close only partly in a year and AI-order estimate momentum is real, so I put the median about 40% of the way (in log terms) from spot toward FV, giving $9.65. That is also close to spot x (1 + base-rate median -10%) = $9.76. Width: a lognormal mixture, 80% at log-sd 0.47 and 20% at 0.70, which sits between the long-run 0.43 and the realized 0.62-0.71. P(>= spot) is 0.41, and the 5th/95th percentiles are $4.10/$22.66. The scenarios are the conditional means of the ladder's bottom quartile, middle half and top quartile ($5.16 / $9.84 / $19.53), so the scenario mean ($11.09) equals the ladder mean. FV ($7.92) is below the ladder median ($9.65) by design: FV is the fundamental anchor, and the ladder allows for the AI-optical premium persisting. Removed as unverifiable on re-check: the Infront Q3 consensus (nokia.com 403), the 'half of AI orders convert within 12 months' quote (transcript not re-opened), and the four earliest earnings-day moves. Research was limited: Twelve Data rate limits, StockAnalysis FY28 values paywalled for CIEN/HPE, and no new web searches were needed beyond source checks. Analyst average PT $14.97 (14 analysts, src 3) is evidence only.
